Mark 14:15 and Luke 22:12 both use the same phrase—a large upper room, furnished and ready. Classical usage included upper floors used for storage or dining. The New Testament restricts it to this significant space where Jesus instituted the Lord's Supper. Translations (Spanish aposento-alto/salón-alto, French chambre-haute) emphasize the room's elevation and size."

  Sense 1: ""
